Adding wind cuts solar + battery storage power costs nearly 20%

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (777 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Solar and battery storage can do a lot of the heavy lifting in a renewable electricity system.
  • Wind fills gaps when solar output drops, so the system needs fewer batteries to keep electricity flowing.
  • Ember’s analysis, produced with the Global Wind Energy Council (GWEC), found that adding wind to solar and battery storage cuts the median cost of meeting 90% of electricity demand from $105 to $86 per megawatt-hour.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Solar and battery storage can do a lot of the heavy lifting in a renewable electricity system. Add wind, and supplying reliable power gets nearly 20% cheaper, according to new analysis from energy think tank Ember.

Wind fills gaps when solar output drops, so the system needs fewer batteries to keep electricity flowing.

Ember’s analysis, produced with the Global Wind Energy Council (GWEC), found that adding wind to solar and battery storage cuts the median cost of meeting 90% of electricity demand from $105 to $86 per megawatt-hour.

The median cost of solar and wind power covering all demand is $89/MWh, with batteries and a little backup.

Solar and wind don’t follow the same schedule. Their output varies by time of day and across seasons, allowing one to offset the other’s shortfalls.

Industry observers note that that matters because storing enough electricity to get through a long stretch of weak solar output gets expensive. Wind reduces the amount of energy the batteries need to store in the first place.

In the US, adding wind reduces the modeled battery requirement to meet 90% of demand from 20 hours of electricity use to 12 hours. Europe sees the same reduction, while China’s requirement falls from 18 hours to 12.

The savings also put cheaper renewable power within reach of more regions. With wind included, regions that account for 75% of global electricity demand can meet 90% of their electricity demand at less than $100/MWh. With solar and batteries alone, that share is only 50%.

“We already know that solar and wind are cheap,” said Daan Walter, principal at Ember.

By combining solar, wind, and batteries, we can deliver reliable power at remarkably low costs almost everywhere in the world. That’s a pretty fundamental shift in the economics of energy.

Recent findings suggest that the researchers also looked at prolonged periods of low output. Globally, weighted by electricity demand, a week of low solar output occurs roughly four times a year. A week in which both solar and wind output are low occurs only about once every four years.

That’s a global average, so individual locations will have different experiences. Ember defines a lull as seven consecutive days of output below half the source’s average.

Combining wind and solar reduces the gaps in low output.

The findings also raise questions for developers planning newly introduced fossil fuel plants.

Ember identifies 845 GW of coal and gas capacity in planning worldwide. Adding wind raises the share located in regions where solar, wind, and battery storage can meet 90% of demand for under $100/MWh from 71% to 90%.

In China alone, wind brings another 91 GW of planned coal and gas capacity into the range where renewables are cheaper.

Industry observers note that include backup to cover all demand, and 706 GW of the planned fossil fuel capacity sits in regions where the renewable-based alternative costs less than $100/MWh. Without wind, that figure falls to 520 GW.

For investors financing fossil fuel plants in the pipeline that are expected to run for decades, there is likely already a cheaper renewable alternative available to meet the same electricity demand, so it’s worth scrutinizing the project’s economics.

Good way to think about the whole system. So what exactly does Don not-Quixote have against windmills?

Ember’s interactive Wind + Solar + Battery Atlas lets people explore reliable electricity costs in their own region.

Tens of millions of crabs are crossing Christmas Island. Here’s how to watch.

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (446 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Popsci

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that the crabs are coming.
  • In a recent development, the migration begins with the first rainfall of the wet season, typically in October or November, but can be as late as December or January.
  • According to Christmas Island National Park, the speed and timing of the migration is determined by the moon’s phases.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that the crabs are coming. Millions upon millions of them. Christmas Island red crabs (Gecarcoidea natalis) have officially begun their annual migration on the tiny Australian territory in the Indian Ocean.

In a recent development, the migration begins with the first rainfall of the wet season, typically in October or November, but can be as late as December or January. Red crabs from all over Christmas Island will leave their homes in the forest at the same time and start their march towards the ocean. Once they reach the ocean, they will mate and spawn. The male crabs lead the migration, while the females join in along the way.

According to Christmas Island National Park, the speed and timing of the migration is determined by the moon’s phases. “Red crabs always spawn before dawn on a receding high-tide during the last quarter of the moon,” the park rangers write. “Incredibly, they know exactly when to leave their burrows to make this lunar date.”.

Sources indicate that however, the crabs will wait until the first rainfall to begin their journey, so they sometimes have to hurry. If the rains arrive close to their optimal spawning date, the crabs will move to the ocean very promptly. If the rain comes early, the crustaceans may take their time, “stopping to eat and drink on their way to the coast.” If rain begins too late to make the spawning date, some of the crabs will remain in their burrows and begin their migration the following month.

It has been revealed that the result is spectacular. Tens of millions of bright red crustaceans the size of a soda can spread out over the 12-mile-wide island on their way to the ocean. They begin their march inland and will reach their destination in about nine days. In 2008, naturalist and documentarian Sir David Attenborough described the annual event as one of his best television moments.

According to recent reports, over the next few days Parks Australia will run livestreams of the migration for about 60 minutes. The exact timing and number of livestreams can’t be scheduled in advance since it is completely dependent on the crabs.

“We will aim to livestream in the morning, but the crabs will have the final say on when and how many days they will venture across the bridge,” the rangers write.

Filming occurs at the red crab bridge, a 16-foot-tall structure built to help the crabs cross the busy road. The crabs will migrate past this bridge for about three to four days.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Take the Swedish maker’s fresh-for-1991 900S convertible.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

From the August 1991 concern of Car and Driver.

Our friend Max has his heart set on a Saab. His brother Pete has a Saab with more than 100,000 miles on it, and Max swears the thing is still as tight as one of Madonna’s bustiers. Max also notes—having read the brochures—that all Saabs now come with more standard equipment than a fire truck. “Seems to me,” says Max, “that no other car gives you as much quality and stuff for the money.”.

Take the Swedish maker’s fresh-for-1991 900S convertible. You’ll note the absence of the word “Turbo” in that moniker. Previously, Saab’s only ragtop was the sprightly turbocharged edition—as nice a convertible as you’ll find, to be sure, but at the moment saddled with a $33,712 stick­er. Oh, and that price busts the $30K luxu­ry-tax barrier, so remember to add another $371 to the bottom line for Uncle Sam.

In a recent development, the new 900S convertible is the “affordable” Saab droptop; it lists for $28,712, no sin tax necessary. Of course, you have to give up something to save $5000-plus. That something is performance. Rather than the Turbo’s 160-horsepow­er 2.0-liter four, the 900S uses a new nor­mally aspirated, twin-cam, sixteen-valve 2.1-liter four-banger that produces 140 horsepower at 6000 rpm and 133 pound­-feet of torque at 2900. (For ’91, this engine is standard in all non-turbo 900 models.) Performance with this powerplant is modest—a run to 60 mph takes 9.6 sec­onds—but that doesn't seem to bother Max. “Hey,” he notes, “not everybody wants to be Ayrton Senna.” In its favor, the engine revs smoothly, with a characteristic Saab whine, and delivers good fuel economy. Our test car turned in a 24-mpg average.

See all results for used cars for sale near 21014.

The rest of the car is a near copy of the Turbo convertible. Which is to say, the 900S is one of the most satisfying sun cars around. The cloth top is power-operated; lowering it is as easy as unlocking two headliner latches and pushing a console­mounted button. With the top down, the body is tight and all but shake-free. Saab attributes the body’s rigidity to its pedigree: the droptop 900S is not a beheaded coupe but a designed-from-the-ground-up soft-top built on a dedicated production line.

As Max has rightly discovered, Saabs justify their sticker prices by being very well equipped. Included in the convertible’s $28,712 base price is everything a discern­ing driver is likely to want: a driver-side air bag; anti-lock brakes; leather seats; power windows, locks, and mirrors; a potent AM/FM/cassette stereo; fog lights; and a headlight wiper/washer system.

In a recent development, if the Saab’s price seems steep com­pared with such convertibles as the Chrysler LeBaron, the Olds Cutlass Supreme, or even the Mazda Miata, bear in mind that few buyers considering the Saab are likely to have those cars on their potential-purchases list. The 900S’s real competitors are such prestige sunsters as the BMW 325i, the Infiniti M30, and even the Cadillac Allanté. The 900S sells for substantially less than all of those, yet it’s on par in terms of refinement, luxury, solidity, and cachet.

See all results for used cars for sale near 21014.

For once, it seems Max has made a decision we can’t argue with.

If you’ve been paying any attention to the shooter market these past few months, you won’t be surprised to learn that Battlefield 6 has been an unprecedented success for EA, and the Battlefield series as a whole.

Industry observers note that the game managed to sell over 7 million units at launch, climbing to the top of the charts anywhere you look, including setting upcoming series concurrent player records on Steam. Thanks to new data, we now better understand the true scale of this launch.

According to recent reports, the latest Circana report, which looks at game and hardware sales in the United States, has arrived. This iteration covers the month of October, which is when Battlefield 6 was released.

It has been revealed that battlefield 6 was the top-selling game across all platforms during October - which isn’t surprising. It has overtaken NBA 2K26 to become 2025’s best-selling game year-to-date, making it the best-selling Battlefield game ever.

In October alone, the game sold more than the lifetime sales of Battlefield 1, previously the best-selling entry in the franchise.

Sources indicate that battlefield 6 even set records beyond just its own series, having now produced the highest single-month dollar sales (physical and digital) total for any full game released in the last three years. The previous record holder was 2022’s Modern Warfare 2.

Recent findings suggest that november’s report, which is set to arrive midway through December, will show, once and for all, whether Battlefield 6 has been able to overtake Black Ops 7. With one exception, Call of Duty games have, for more than a decade, topped the best-selling year-to-date chart. Regardless of the quality of the individual titles, or the competition in any given year, nothing has been able to shake that dominance.

Recent findings suggest that given all this momentum, Battlefield 6 has a shot at dethroning Call of Duty this year, beating Black Ops 7 to become the year’s best-seller. You never want to count out the sheer popularity of Call of Duty among casual players, however, which is what’s going to make December’s report all the more interesting.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • In a recent development, at South Korea’s Daegu Gyeongbuk Institute of Science and Technology (DGIST), engineer and study co-author Soon Moon Jeong believes the underlying dynamics at play are a promising upcoming way to analyze and pinpoint deformations in a soft robot.
  • Jeong’s team first designed a thin but resilient “tubular mechanoluminescent fiber” made from glowing particles of zinc sulfide and flexible polymers.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, A tiny, four-limbed soft robot resembling the cross between an octopus and an earthworm does more than inch across difficult terrain. With a process known as mechanoluminescence, the device glows as it moves and stretches without the need for external batteries or electronics. It’s not flimsy, either. Writing in a study recently published in the journal Small Structures, the soft robot’s inventors explained their design maintains its illuminating abilities after more than 1,000 stretching cycles.

In a recent development, at South Korea’s Daegu Gyeongbuk Institute of Science and Technology (DGIST), engineer and study co-author Soon Moon Jeong believes the underlying dynamics at play are a promising upcoming way to analyze and pinpoint deformations in a soft robot. It’s also potentially even more effective than existing softer options, since it doesn’t require additional components that might otherwise restrict the device’s movement.

Jeong’s team first designed a thin but resilient “tubular mechanoluminescent fiber” made from glowing particles of zinc sulfide and flexible polymers. They then filled elastic silicone tubes with the mixture, and wove them together into a mesh-like case for their pneumatic soft robot model. As the robot’s limbs stretch and contract, the zinc sulfide-infused polymer filling glows bright green specifically in the areas undergoing stress. Laboratory testing indicated their novel fibers withstood being pulled over twice their original length, and kept glowing after over 1,000 exercises.

It has been revealed that jeong said his team is now focusing on improving the robot’s light emissions and resiliency. If successful, their mechanoluminescent fibers may be used in wearable medical devices or even artificial skins.

“The woven fiber-network configuration provides qualitative visual indication of deformation over the robotic body, offering a simple strategy for realizing self-visualizing soft robotic systems,” wrote the study’s authors, adding that their invention showcases the potential foundations for “next-generation self-visualizing intelligent soft systems.”.

#41082. When Violence Is the Point

When Violence Is the Point

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1429 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Psychologytoday

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Updated November 20, 2026 | Reviewed by Lybi Ma.
  • On January 4, 2025, a 14-year-old boy in Borås, Sweden, walked up to a 55-year-old woman who was out walking her dog and stabbed her.
  • According to recent reports, the attack wasn’t his idea.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Updated November 20, 2026 | Reviewed by Lybi Ma.

By Avery Ellis and H. Colleen Sinclair, Ph.D.

On January 4, 2025, a 14-year-old boy in Borås, Sweden, walked up to a 55-year-old woman who was out walking her dog and stabbed her. He streamed the attack live on Discord to an online group he desperately wanted to join.

According to recent reports, the attack wasn’t his idea. The group first gave him an initiation task: Slash car tires. When he did, they told him it wasn’t enough. Find a human target, they noted. The woman survived after two surgeries. Streaming viewers tipped off police, who arrested the boy that evening. When asked why he did it, he said he wanted to belong.

Sources indicate that was this extremism? A random assault? A gang initiation? Child exploitation? Unsettlingly, it may be all four. U.S. law enforcement has a name for this kind of threat: nihilistic violent extremism, or NVE, a label the FBI and Department of Justice introduced in 2025. It describes loosely connected online networks, many of them branching out of a sprawling ecosystem called the Com (short for “the community”).

Recent findings suggest that this ecosystem is also linked to TCC, the “True Crime Community,” dark fandoms (soon to be featured on 60 Minutes). But unlike the images that the TCC descriptor might bring to mind of keyboard sleuths obsessed with crime documentaries, these individuals are more interested in committing than solving crime. Their modus operandi is recruiting young people through gaming platforms and social media sites to push them toward harming themselves and others. It is grooming for violence.

The threat is growing fast. The Polarization and Extremism Research and Innovation Lab (PERIL) counted eight NVE-linked plots and attacks worldwide in 2023. By mid-November 2026, it had counted 69 for the year, an increase of 763 percent (Jensen, 2026). Schools were the most common target, and outside the United States, the median perpetrator age was just 16.

These threats take more than one form. Just this month, Bavarian authorities arrested two teenagers from the German state of Hesse. They are suspected members of the Com who pressured three girls aged 13 and 14 into filming sexual acts and self-harm (News.de, 2026).

A stabbing in Sweden and online sextortion in Germany look like very different crimes, yet both fall under the same label. That is part of the problem. Researchers, police, schools, and tech platforms all use the term NVE, but they don’t always mean the same thing. Here is where they appear to agree versus where they don’t.

Hatred of humanity in general. A recent review of NVE definitions found that most share a small set of core elements (Zdjelar, 2026), and misanthropy leads the list. Unlike prejudice aimed at a specific group, misanthropy is hatred of people in general. The group No Lives Matter calls ordinary people “mundane” and urges members to spread “terror to all who are mundane.” One recruiter put out a call for “true misanthropic individuals” (Njohsp).

Status earned through harm. The second widely shared feature is clout-chasing: gaining attention and rank by committing cruelty, or coercing others to do so. Leaked chat archives from 764, one of the most notorious NVE networks, show a hierarchy in which members climb by producing violent content (Argentino, 2025). Victims, often young girls, are groomed, pressured into sending explicit images, and then extorted into harming themselves on camera. That footage is collected in “lorebooks” that circulate through the network to control victims and raise the status of perpetrators (Hwang, 2026). The harm is the content, and the content is the currency.

In a recent development, young people recruiting young people. NVE participants are overwhelmingly young, and so are their victims. Across Com-linked arrests worldwide, the median offender is 19, and the median victim is 13 (Argentino and Lindsay, 2026). Recruitment happens on the platforms where teenagers already spend their time.

Industry observers note that is there an ideology? The word “nihilistic” suggests these groups believe in nothing, and some researchers agree, describing NVE as violence without a clear ideological motive (ISD, 2025). Others argue that nihilism has become an ideology of its own, with rules and justifications for violence (Gill, 2025). Still others see a “salad bar” of borrowed imagery, such as Nazi symbols, Satanism, and school-shooter fandom, used for shock value rather than belief (Argentino and Lindsay, 2026; Sivignon, 2026). The evidence cuts both ways. A study of 29 adjudicated Com-network cases found that genuine ideological motives did appear in some pathways to offline violence, but often only after violent tendencies were already present (Clemmow and colleagues, 2026).

Is the violence a means to an end? The FBI’s definition indicates NVEs seek to bring about society’s collapse. Some groups at the edge of this ecosystem fit that description. The Order of Nine Angles (O9A), a satanic neo-Nazi movement, promotes ritual “culling” of people it deems worthless as a path to societal breakdown (Gartenstein-Ross, 2025). Other researchers argue that most NVE actors have no strategic goal and that chaos is the point (Argentino and Lindsay, 2026). Whether groups like O9A fall under the NVE umbrella, or are better understood as accelerationists, is debatable.

Is copycatting a defining feature? Many NVE attackers idolize earlier killers. PERIL found documented veneration of past attackers, most often in online tribute posts, in 62 percent of NVE plots and attacks. Columbine alone was cited in 88 cases across 20 countries (Jensen, 2026). In some online dark fandoms, mass shooters are called “saints.” Yet sextortion networks like the one implicated in Germany may never reference a past attack. Is veneration a core of NVE, or the signature of one branch of it?

Sources indicate that where does NVE end and something else begin? NVE overlaps with a crowd of related labels: the True Crime Community, sadistic online exploitation, participatory memetic violent extremism, and “mixed, unclear, and unstable” ideologies, to name a few. Some researchers treat these as parts of a single NVE ecosystem. Others see distinct problems that call for distinct responses.

Sources indicate that debating definitions can sound like academic hair-splitting. It isn’t. A school counselor, a prosecutor, and a content moderator can look at the same teenager and see three different problems: a mental health crisis, a criminal, a terms-of-service violation. Define the threat too narrowly, and we miss the warning signs. Define it too broadly, and the label sweeps in kids who need help, not handcuffs. Many of the young people involved are both victims and perpetrators.

NVEs pose a rapidly growing and increasingly alarming threat to youth worldwide. Despite the groups’ definitional ambiguity, experts largely agree that misanthropy and clout-chasing sit at the core of nihilistic violent extremism. Other definitional elements are still being debated. Experts should work toward definitional agreement and do so promptly. After all, a threat left undefined is a threat left unchecked.

Co-author Avery Ellis is a psychology student at Louisiana State University.

If you’re worried a child is being targeted or extorted online, report it to the National Center for Missing & Exploited Children’s CyberTipline at report.cybertip.org or 1-800-843-5678. If someone is in crisis, call or text 988.

What are the potential pitfalls of shifting cross-border trade deals? What if a really popular video game comes out and everybody takes Thursday off?

Sources indicate that that last snag might sound ridiculous, but according to a survey from staffing software tech giant BambooHR, nearly 20 percent of salaried U.S. workers are planning on taking the day off on Thursday, November 19, to play the newly introduced Grand Theft Auto VI game, which will launch at midnight (ET). Dwight Schrute would be furious.

According to recent reports, hype over GTA VI has been building steadily over the past few years, stoked by a couple of delays. Reportedly, presales of the game have hit the billion-dollar mark, which means that there are going to be a lot of sore thumbs over the next while.

For non-gamers, all of this furor can be hard to digest. However, in terms of storytelling, video gaming has proved a strong competitor for the movie industry, capable of weaving plot lines that extend over hours and hours of gameplay. Sure, nobody agonized over the paddle’s motivation in Pong, but these days you can make both a game and a movie about two Italian plumbers battling turtles, and both film and game will rake in huge profits.

It has been revealed that early reviews for the game are out, and the critics are almost universal in a chorus of praise for the blend of immersion and action, and the way the world of Vice City seems to be alive. The graphics look incredible, and unlike with some previous large gaming releases, the bugs seem to have been worked out in those previous launch delays.

Besides all the Grand Theft stuff, the Autos part of the series looks to be better than ever. Beyond police-spec Ford Explorer and Taurus Interceptors, there will be supercars, Rolls-Royce cabriolets, and all manner of high-dollar fare that you can nab on a whim. GTA VI doesn’t brand these cars, so it’ll be something called a Pegassi that you’ll be streaking down the highway in rather than a Lamborghini, but the looks are virtually the same.

The GTA series has always been slightly controversial for its blend of crime and violence, but then again, Goodfellas wasn’t popular as just a film about Joe Pesci offering art criticism on a painting with two dogs in it. Virtually robbing a bank and launching your getaway car over an apartment building is good fun, and it helps to blow off a little steam after a stressful day at work.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that we may earn revenue from the products available on this page and participate in affiliate programs. Learn more ›.

Someone doesn’t have to be great at cooking to enjoy it. Having the right gear really helps, though, and that creates a wellspring of great gifting opportunities. The HORL3 Cruise holds a knife against a magnet at a fixed 15- or 20-degree angle while a diamond disc rolls along the edge. The ThermoWorks Thermapen Nano gets a reading in about 0.4 seconds, so anyone can stop guessing when a roast is done. The Challenger Bread Pan traps steam under a tall cast-iron lid, the same trick bakeries pull off with steam-injected ovens. Every pick below works on that principle, helping the home cook elevate their kitchen experience.

Sources indicate that there are dozens and dozens of gifts here, grouped by category. Jump to: precision and measurement, knives and sharpening, pans and cookware, coffee, tea and drinks, baking and from scratch, countertop appliances, plus sauces and cookbooks.

Industry observers note that seasoning a thick steak with a typical pepper grinder takes a lot of twisting. The MÄNNKITCHEN Pepper Cannon uses hardened high-carbon stainless steel burrs spinning on a drive shaft supported by two bearings inside a body milled from a solid block of anodized aluminum. MÄNNKITCHEN claims 10 times the output of top-rated mills, which it describes as seven cranks instead of 70. You set the grind from 8 to 60+ mesh with an adjuster on the base that clicks into spring-loaded detents. The hopper holds half a cup of peppercorns, and a removable cup underneath catches up to a third of a cup of ground pepper, which is handy when a rub calls for a measured amount.

A major mixing bowl tends to hide a kitchen scale’s display right when you need to read it. On the OXO Good Grips 11 lb Stainless Steel Food Scale with Pull-Out Display, the readout sits on a tray that slides out from the base, clear of whatever’s on the platform, then tucks back in for storage. It weighs up to 11 pounds (5 kilograms), and a meter on the display shows how much capacity you have left as you add ingredients. The display has an optional backlight, and the stainless steel platform lifts off so you can wash it by hand.

Sous vide cooking holds a water bath at the exact temperature you want your food to finish at, so a steak can sit in it and stay medium-rare instead of drifting toward well-done. The Anova Precision Cooker 3.0 heats that bath with an 1,100-watt element and circulates 8 liters of water per minute, and Anova rates it to hold within 0.2°F anywhere from 32°F to 197°F. A two-line touchscreen on the cooker shows time and temperature, and dual-band Wi-Fi lets you start or check a cook from your phone. Anova gives it an IPX7 water-resistance rating, and the clamp adjusts and detaches to fit different pots.

It has been revealed that thermoWorks has closed out the Thermapen One, and the Thermapen Nano took its place this year. ThermoWorks rates the Nano’s fixed thermocouple probe for a full reading in 0.4 seconds and accuracy within 0.5°F between -4°F and 248°F, a window that covers everything from rare beef to pulled pork. Two magnets built into the body let it ride on the side of the fridge or range hood, and the display rotates a full 360 degrees, so the numbers read right-side up whichever hand you hold it in. It’s IP67 rated, runs roughly 1,000 hours on one AAA battery, and comes with a five-year warranty and a NIST-traceable calibration certificate.

Recent findings suggest that A fast thermocouple thermometer doesn’t have to cost triple digits. TempPro, the brand formerly known as ThermoPro, builds a thermocouple sensor into the TempSwift Pro TP622 and rates it for a 0.1-second response time and accuracy within 0.5°F across -58°F to 572°F. That high end reaches past meat into frying oil and candy-making territory. The backlit display auto-rotates 180 degrees for left- or right-handed use, and the thermometer wakes up when you lift it and goes to sleep after 90 seconds of sitting still. It carries an IP65 water-resistance rating and runs on a single AAA battery.

Recent findings suggest that the Combustion Predictive Thermometer (2nd Gen) is built around the question people actually ask during a roast: how much longer? Its probe carries eight sensors along its length, so the app can show the core, the surface and the air temperature around the food at the same time. Combustion’s prediction engine uses that heat-flow data to estimate the time remaining, and a feature it calls TrueCore reports the lowest internal reading even if you didn’t hit the center. Combustion rates the upper half of the probe to 900°F, so it can stay in a roast under the broiler or on the grill. Bluetooth reaches more than 330 feet in open air, and Wi-Fi requires a separate booster accessory.

Freehand sharpening is hard mostly because holding a steady angle is hard. The HORL3 Cruise takes that job off your hands: a magnetic block holds the knife at either 15 or 20 degrees, and you roll a wheel with a diamond disc back and forth along the edge. The other end of the roller carries a stainless steel honing disc to straighten and refine the edge you just ground. The Cruise’s body is made from ocean-bound recycled plastic, and HORL builds it in Germany. If the person you’re shopping for would rather have wood on the counter, the $179 HORL3 uses an oak or walnut body and swaps in an interchangeable ceramic disc.

According to recent reports, STEELPORT forges its 8-inch Chef Knife from a single billet of American 52100 carbon steel in Portland, Oregon, then heat treats the edge and spine differently. The company claims the edge ends up around 65 HRC, hard enough to take and hold a fine edge, while the spine stays below 30 HRC so the blade as a whole is less brittle. The handle is resin-stabilized Oregon bigleaf maple burl, and a magnetic walnut sheath comes in the box. Carbon steel picks up a patina and can rust, so wipe it dry after every wash. STEELPORT covers the knife with a lifetime warranty and sharpens it free for as long as you own it.

Sources indicate that A knife that suddenly feels dull often has an edge that’s just rolled over, and a few passes on a honing rod push it back into line between real sharpenings. STEELPORT’s 12-Inch Oval Ceramic Honing Rod does that with a fine-grit ceramic surface over a steel core. The oval cross-section is there for contact, and STEELPORT notes it puts more of the blade against the rod than a round one does. The rod measures 17 inches overall with a 5-inch contoured walnut handle and a finger guard, and it weighs 12 ounces. Ceramic can crack if it hits a tile floor, so give it a hook or its own drawer slot.

According to recent reports, shun builds the Classic 8-Inch Chef’s Knife around a VG-MAX steel core clad in 34 layers of stainless Damascus on each side, which is where the rippled pattern on the blade comes from. The core is hardened to 60-61 on the Rockwell scale and hand-sharpened to about 16 degrees per side, a fine edge that slices through onions and herbs cleanly. The full-tang blade sits in a D-shaped black PakkaWood handle, and the whole knife weighs 7.5 ounces. Shun makes it in Seki, Japan. A hard, thin edge like this one is happiest on a wood or plastic board, and it shouldn’t go anywhere near bones or frozen food.

Softer stainless steel is quicker to bring back to a sharp edge, and that’s part of the appeal of the Made In 8-Inch Chef Knife. It’s fully forged in Thiers, France, from nitrogen-treated X50CrMoV15 stainless hardened to 58+ HRC, so a few passes on a whetstone or rolling sharpener refresh it. Made In grinds the edge asymmetrically, with a 14-degree primary bevel on one side and a 4-degree polishing bevel on the other, for 18 degrees total. The blade actually measures 8.5 inches and the knife weighs 7 ounces. If you order directly from Made In, the company will engrave it for $30 more, but engraved knives can’t be returned.

It has been revealed that someone outfitting a first real kitchen needs a handful of good knives more than a block with 15 slots. The Cangshan N1 Series 6-Piece Knife Block Set forges its blades from German X50CrMoV15 stainless hardened to 58 HRC, a steel that’s easy to touch up at home. The N1’s signature is its patented all-metal hollow handle, which runs straight out of the blade, so there are no wood or plastic scales to crack or loosen. Cangshan sells the set under more than one model number, so check the knife list on the listing before you order.

Tojiro has renamed its long-running DP line to Classic, but the F-808 210mm gyuto itself didn’t change. It’s a san mai blade, with a VG10 stainless core hardened to about 60 HRC sandwiched between softer stainless outer layers that add toughness around the hard cutting steel. The 50/50 double-bevel edge suits right- and left-handed cooks equally, and the Western-style handle has a full tang, a stainless bolster and three rivets, so it’ll feel familiar to anyone coming from a German knife. Tojiro makes it in Tsubame-Sanjo, Japan. The edge measures 212 millimeters and the knife weighs 7.2 ounces.

Learning to sharpen on a stone starts with two grits, and the King KW-65 puts both on one block. The 1000-grit side does the sharpening and raises a fresh edge, then the 6000-grit side polishes it. It’s a soaking stone, so you submerge it for a couple of minutes before you start and keep it wet while you work. The muddy slurry that builds up on the surface helps it cut, so leave it there rather than rinsing it away mid-session. The stone measures about 7.3 by 2.5 by 1 inches, sits in an included plastic stand, and is made in Japan.

Industry observers note that the deep, 6-quart sauté pan at the center of the All-Clad NS Pro Ceramic Nonstick VIP comes with a steamer insert, a roasting rack and a tempered glass lid, so one piece of cookware can sear and steam on the stovetop or roast in the oven. The body is hard-anodized recycled aluminum, and a stainless steel base bonded underneath makes it work on induction burners. The ceramic nonstick interior is oven-safe to 450°F, though the lid tops out at 350°F and the pan can’t go under the broiler. Wash it by hand, and know that All-Clad’s warranty on this pan runs one year.

Carbon steel seasons and sears like cast iron, and it heats up and cools down faster when you adjust the burner. Made In’s Seasoned Carbon Steel Frying Pan arrives pre-seasoned with shea nut and coconut oils, so you can start cooking in it sooner than you could with a bare pan. The 12-inch size weighs 4.31 pounds, with a 9.25-inch cooking surface and 2.25-inch sides. Made In builds it in Sweden, rates it for heat up to 1,200°F, and states it works on induction and over an open fire. The hollow stainless handle is designed to stay cool, and the pan should be washed by hand and dried right away.

Sources indicate that smithey is better known for cast iron, but its Deep Farmhouse Skillet is hand-forged carbon steel, made in Charleston, South Carolina. It’s about 12 inches across the top and 2 inches deep, which leaves room for a pan sauce or a shallow fry, and the cooking surface measures about 9.5 inches. Long handles on both sides stretch it to almost 21 inches end to end, so you can carry all 6 pounds of it to the table with two hands. Smithey lists it for use on gas, induction, electric and open fire.

Sources indicate that smithey’s 7.25 QT Dutch Oven skips enamel entirely. It’s bare cast iron with a fully polished interior, pre-seasoned with grapeseed oil, so it builds up seasoning the same way a skillet does and there’s no enamel coating to chip. The domed lid has drip channels on its underside that send condensation back down onto the food during a long braise. Expect some heft, since it weighs about 17.3 pounds with the lid. Smithey makes it in the US and backs it with a lifetime guarantee. Bare iron doesn’t love long simmers in tomato or wine, so save those braises for an enameled pot or keep them short.

Old cast iron is prized for its smooth, machined cooking surfaces, and Lancaster Cast Iron’s No. 8 Skillet brings that finish to a latest pan. The cooking surface is polished smooth, then pre-seasoned with two layers of grapeseed oil at the company’s shop in Lancaster, Pennsylvania. The No. 8 measures 10.5 inches across the top, with a 9.25-inch cooking surface and 2-inch walls, and it weighs about 4 pounds. Polished iron starts out slick, and it gets slicker as layers of seasoning build up with every cook.

Recent findings suggest that cooking pancakes in a skillet is a solitary affair. If you’re the cook and don’t want to force cold coasters on everyone, you’re standing alone and eating last. Unless you have this newly introduced griddle, that is. This 12-pound rectangle spans two burners and stays put, providing an 18.5-by-9.8-inch cooking surface and two heat zones, so you can cook a bunch of pancakes, or eggs and bacon, simultaneously, which means everyone eats together. The carbon steel is nitrided, which means it resists rust and scratches without the need for questionable coatings. Plus, it arrives pre-seasoned with a surface that will only become more non-stick with proper use and care. Plus, a raised lip and rounded corners keep grease in while making it easy to pour off. It’s a great choice whether you’re cooking at the stovetop, in an oven, on a grill, or over a campfire.

A saucier’s rounded bottom leaves no corners for a whisk or spatula to miss, which makes it the pan for custard and polenta and anything else that likes to scorch where the wall meets the floor. The Misen 3 QT Stainless Steel Saucier is 5-ply, with aluminum layers sandwiched inside stainless steel to spread heat across the base, and the walls are 3 millimeters thick. It measures about 9 inches across, comes with a lid, works on induction, and is oven-safe to 800°F. Misen backs it with a lifetime warranty against defects.

Kuhn Rikon’s 4th Burner Pot is tall and narrow, 5.5 inches across and holding 12 cups, so it fits on the small back burner while bigger pans take the front of the stove. That makes it handy for a couple of servings of pasta or a batch of blanched green beans. The glass lid has two built-in strainers and a pour spout, which lets you drain without hauling out a colander, and a removable basket inside handles steaming. Interior measurement marks save you a measuring cup, the silicone handles stay cool, and the stainless pot works on induction.

Microwave cooking goes better when steam is managed, and that’s the idea behind the Anyday 8-Piece Glass Round Dish Set. Each borosilicate glass dish gets a tempered glass lid with a silicone vent and gasket that let steam build and escape while the food cooks. Anyday notes the stainless steel rim on each lid is microwave-safe as long as the dish sits at least an inch from the microwave’s walls. The set includes four dishes: two 4-cup sizes, one shallow and one deep, plus a 7-cup and an 8-cup. The bowls can go in the oven up to 500°F, so leftovers can get a crisp finish after they reheat.

Sources indicate that green tea scorches at a full boil, and pour-over coffee likes water a few degrees below it. The Fellow Corvo EKG Pro lets you dial in anywhere from 104 to 212 degrees Fahrenheit, then hold that temperature for 15 to 60 minutes so the second cup is as hot as the first. It also has an altitude setting, scheduling, and a pre-boil sanitize mode. The 0.9-liter body is 304 stainless steel. Fellow says the Wi-Fi only handles firmware updates, so you’ll still set the temperature on the kettle itself rather than from your phone.

Uneven grounds make uneven coffee, because the fine bits over-extract while the big chunks barely give up any flavor. The Fellow Ode Brew Grinder Gen 2 uses 64 mm stainless steel flat burrs, which cut a more uniform particle than the blade grinders most people start with. You get 11 settings split into 31 steps, a 100-gram capacity, and anti-static tech to keep grounds from clinging to the catch cup. Fellow built it for drip, pour-over, French press, and cold brew. It isn’t designed for espresso, so skip it for anyone pulling shots at home.

Recent findings suggest that A coffee maker can only brew as well as its water temperature allows. The Moccamaster KBGV Select, handmade in the Netherlands, heats water quickly to brewing temperature with a copper boiling element, and the hot plate runs on its own separate element so it doesn’t cook the coffee sitting in the carafe. A switch on the brew basket adjusts the flow for a full 10-cup pot or a half batch, which keeps small batches from coming out thin. It carries the Specialty Coffee Association’s certification and a five-year warranty.

Most of the frustration of home espresso comes from dosing and grinding by feel. The Ninja Luxe Café Premier handles both: it has a conical burr grinder with 25 settings and a built-in scale that weighs the grounds for you, so each shot starts from a consistent dose. The Dual Froth System has four hands-free presets for steamed or frothed milk, and the machine also makes drip-style coffee and cold brew. It suits someone who wants café drinks without learning to tamp and time shots by eye.

So you know someone with a grinder, a pour-over cone, a French press, a cold brew pitcher, and a milk frother. But sometimes they need a coffee before they can face making coffee. And that’s where this indulgently overengineered Swiss superautomatic espresso maker comes in. The second-generation Z10 has a menu of 51 drinks you can choose and customize through the 4.3-inch touchscreen. Just pour beans into the hopper and fill the water tank. Drinks include classic hot options, as well as “cold brew,” which, while not true long-immersion, is still nice for ice thanks to unheated water pulsing through a coarser grind. With milk or without. But now there are also light selections, plus caffeine regulation levels, as well as sweet foam picks (with a $35 chocolate attachment sold separately). And the upgraded P.R.G.2+ grinder resets itself for each offering, dialing in optimized granule consistency so you never have to worry you’ll have bad luck with a puck. Sure, it’s a splurge, but think of all the time and space someone will save replacing all those other coffee contraptions.

Most countertop carbonators tell you to fizz plain water and add flavor afterward, because carbonating juice or wine tends to foam over. The Drinkmate OmniFizz gets around that with what the company calls its Fizz Infuser cap, which releases pressure gradually so you can carbonate cold drinks other than water. It runs on standard 60-liter CO2 cylinders, and Drinkmate sells it alone or in bundles with extra cylinders. Check the bundles before buying, since the kits with more cylinders were sometimes cheaper than the smaller ones in early November.

Matcha powder starts losing its color and flavor once it’s ground, which is why the Cuzen Matcha Maker grinds whole tea leaves on demand. Its hopper holds up to 20 grams of leaf, and the machine mills it, then mixes it with water in the cup using a magnetic whisk. You can pick a 1-, 1.5-, or 2-gram shot depending on how strong you like it, and there’s a grind-only mode for baking or lattes. The Starter Kit comes with 4-gram samples of three Cuzen leaf blends and a brush for cleaning the mill.

Pod-based cocktail machines lock you into one organization’s drinks. The Barsys 360 uses whatever you put in it: six 750-milliliter canisters hold your own spirits, juices, and syrups, and a Bluetooth app tells the machine how much of each to pour through the spouts over the glass. It doesn’t shake or stir, so plan on finishing drinks the old-fashioned way. It also runs on USB-C power and weighs about 10 pounds empty, which makes it easier than you’d expect to move from the counter to a party table.

Sources indicate that nugget ice, the soft, chewable kind, is made by compressing ice flakes rather than freezing cubes in a tray. The GoveeLife Smart Nugget Ice Maker Pro does that on your counter, and Govee rates it for up to 60 pounds a day, with the first batch ready in about six minutes. A 4.9-liter side tank supplements the 2.2-liter main reservoir so you refill less often, and it has two self-cleaning cycles. You can also check on it or start it from the Govee app or by voice with Alexa or Google.

In a recent development, centrifugal juicers spin produce against a fast blade, while slow juicers like the Hurom H310 Easy Clean press it with a turning screw at roughly 45 rotations per minute. Hurom’s version has a self-feeding hopper with a 50-millimeter chute that the company states fits whole apples, which cuts down on prep. Hurom backs the 150-watt motor with a 10-year warranty and covers the other parts for two years.

Boxed wine stays fresh longer than an open bottle, but the cardboard box is nobody’s idea of a centerpiece. The Boxxle Box Wine Dispenser is a stainless steel and ABS plastic housing for the bag inside a standard box. According to Boxxle, it lifts the bag so the spout sits above your glass and presses on the bag as it empties, so you can keep pouring until the last glass.

Fresh pasta dough needs to be rolled thin and evenly, and doing it with a rolling pin takes practice most people don’t have. The Marcato Atlas 150 is a hand-cranked roller with a 10-position thickness dial, so you can step the dough down a little at a time until it’s thin enough for lasagna sheets. The rollers are anodized aluminum, and the body is chrome-plated steel made in Italy. The version sold in the US includes fettuccine and spaghetti cutters, so you can go from sheet to noodles without buying attachments.

Most stand mixers drive a beater from above. The Ankarsrum Assistent Original flips that: its motor sits in the base and spins the 7-liter stainless steel bowl itself, while a dough hook or roller stays put. That design is why Ankarsrum says it can knead up to 5 kilograms of dough, a load that would stall a lot of tilt-head mixers. The Essential Package comes with a dough roller, dough knife, dough hook, spatula, and a proofing lid. Ankarsrum covers the base with a seven-year warranty, though accessories aren’t included.

Bread machines have a reputation for pale, unevenly baked tops. The Zojirushi Home Bakery Virtuoso Plus adds a heater in the lid to go with the usual one underneath, so the top of the loaf browns along with the sides. It bakes a 2-pound loaf and uses two kneading blades, which helps it work a full 2-pound batch of dough evenly.

Industry observers note that sourdough gets its crackly crust from steam trapped around the loaf early in the bake, which is why so many bakers use a Dutch oven. The Challenger Bread Pan rearranges that idea: you set the dough on a shallow cast-iron base and lower a tall domed lid over it, so you’re not dropping a floppy loaf into a deep, 500-degree pot. It weighs 20 pounds, is made in the USA, and is rated to 500 degrees Fahrenheit. Its 15.5-by-10.5-inch footprint fits oblong batards as well as round boules.

Industry observers note that hexClad’s hybrid surface finally made the jump from frying pans to the oven. The HexClad Hybrid Baking Sheets use the same pattern of raised stainless steel hexagons with nonstick valleys in between, built over 2.5-millimeter tri-ply with an aluminum core. HexClad says the ceramic coating is free of PFAS and rates the sheets for oven temperatures up to 900 degrees Fahrenheit. They’re sold in two-packs in small and medium sizes, and the medium sheet measures 10 by 15 inches. HexClad says they’re dishwasher-safe but recommends washing them by hand.

Detroit-style pizza owes its crunchy, cheese-crisped edges to a deep rectangular pan that conducts heat fast. The LloydPans 10×14 Detroit-Style Pizza Pan is 2.5 inches deep and made from 14-gauge anodized aluminum in Spokane Valley, Washington. Its Pre-Seasoned Tuff-Kote finish means you can skip seasoning and use metal utensils on it, according to LloydPans. Spread the cheese all the way to the edges so it melts down the sides and fries against the metal.

Stretching pizza dough on a countertop usually ends with flour everywhere. The Gozney Pizza Prep Board has raised edges that keep the flour on the board and a catch tray at the back where you can sweep extra flour and reuse it. Its textured surface holds a thin, even coating of flour, which Gozney says works better than wood, steel, or marble at keeping dough from sticking and tearing on its way to the peel. A bench hook keeps it from sliding, and size markings go up to 16 inches. It’s 22 by 21.5 inches, so check counter space first.

Neapolitan pizza wants a stone near 850 degrees Fahrenheit, a temperature home ovens don’t reach. The Ooni Volt 2, successor to the Volt 12, gets there on a standard 120-volt outlet in about 20 minutes, according to Ooni. Inside is a 10-millimeter cordierite stone sized for 12-inch pizzas, and Ooni’s Pizza Intelligence system shifts power between the heating elements as you cook. Presets cover Neapolitan, thin and crispy, and pan pizza. At about 39 pounds, it’s heavy enough that you’ll want to give it a permanent spot.

In a recent development, chef Nancy Silverton started with a quarter sheet pan when she helped Made In design this dish, then stretched it longer and wider. The Made In Porcelain Baking Slab is a 9-by-13-inch French porcelain dish fired three times in the Loire Valley, with a lower profile than a typical casserole so roasted vegetables and gratins get more browning. It’s oven-safe to 650 degrees Fahrenheit and microwave-safe, and it weighs 3.8 pounds. Made In’s care guide claims it can go in the dishwasher, though the company’s FAQ recommends hand washing.

In a recent development, most microwaves cook by guesswork, and the most interaction you have is five beeps and the sighs/screams when things are too cold in the middle and hot at the edges. This sleek Japanese Microwave from Panasonic, however, uses its upcoming Genius Sensor 2.0 to constantly measure 64 points on your food’s surface every 0.1 seconds, so one button push can achieve even temperature throughout a plate of mixed leftovers. And steady inverter power ensures the center heats, too. The drop-down door, like a wall oven, suits even a narrow galley kitchen (aka many Asian apartments), while the flat, turntable-free interior can fit up to a 9-by-13 dish. This recent import is a 2026 Red Dot Design winner for a reason: it’s got a look as tasty as your bowl of steamy soup.

Want that perfectly fluffy restaurant rice at home, but without under- or over-cooking anxiety and hot-spot drama? Get a Zojirushi rice cooker. I’ve given the NS-ZCC10 Neuro Fuzzy Logic model as a graduation/housewarming gift multiple times because I knew from personal experience it delivers year after year. Then I got this pressure + induction cooker in 2025 and daaaaaaamn … somehow the best got better. Sticky-plump sushi or stir-fry grains, pleasingly textured oatmeal, brown rice that doesn’t take all of eternity. No sad, beige cement. This tiny, calm chef quietly adjusts the heat to deliver evenly cooked everything. It’s not as fast as some cookers, but it beats them in consistency. Fill to the line, press a button, go live life, come back to perfection. This is an upgrade that quietly, magically improves your entire kitchen rhythm.

We’ve wasted so many herbs. You buy basil with such good intentions, but two recipes and three days later, there’s still so much that’s wilted and wasted. Same can be said for other greens. And maybe you know someone in the same situation. One “simple” solution is for them to grow their own greens, but not everyone has room for a garden. And what about winter … Well, that’s where this egg-shaped enclosure comes in. Using NASA-inspired nutrient-infused fogponics (way more exciting to watch than standard hydroponics), anyone can grow lettuce or kale or cherry tomatoes, etc., from pre-seeded pods/reusable germination domes, and do it year-round. Just put the indoor garden in a side room, garage, basement, etc., (grow lights can get pretty bright), connect it to Wi-Fi with the Plantaform app, and give it water when an alert tells you. Then, in a few weeks, harvest time! Seasonings season! Garnishes galore! Just clean it well, and you’ll be able to keep good produce on the cutting board, not in the compost. Literally rinse and repeat.

Sources indicate that coffee nerds have so much in common with audiophiles. Both are obsessed with micro-calibrated gear and swapping components in and out in the pursuit of clarity. So if you know someone as obsessed with puck preparation as they are running a carbon-fiber anti-static brush over every album, you know someone who needs the Mazzer Philos premium light commercial single-dose grinder. Like a summit-fi digital audio converter, this $1,495 hand-assembled, heirloom-quality Italian appliance (available in black and silver) takes whatever beans it’s fed and extracts previously masked tasting notes with minimal morning commotion. A wide dial covers espresso to pour-over to batch brew coarseness, and the near-zero-retention vertical burr + chute knocker + Dose Finisher system lets you move between origins and brewing methods without yesterday’s beans staging a comeback. Swappable 64mm flat burrs give someone a chance to tune for vibrant light and full-bodied dark roasts, and the option to switch from stepped to stepless mode gives grind settings the same obsessive precision as establishing the perfect listening position.

Recent findings suggest that south Korea isn’t a casual getaway. But you can still get some Seoul in your soul (food) at home with this set of sauces from three-Michelin-star chef Mingoo Kang of Mingles restaurant and James Beard Award winner Nadia Cho. Fermented slowly in onggi (traditional Korean clay jars that are buried in the hills), and branded with the Korean word for artisan, these sauces are so much better than the red plastic tub of industrial soybean-chili paste you’d pick up at the store (but I still got love for you, H Mart). Start by stirring the deep heat of cooking sauce into marinades, dressings, and/or broths, then use the finishing sauce to glaze meats, or drizzle some zest onto eggs, rice, or dumplings. Whether a chef you know prefers marinara or bibimbap, give them the gift of earthenware alchemy.

Nik Sharma’s newest book builds its 100 recipes around the science of flavor, explaining why each technique works. Fundamentals of Flavor: 100 Recipes for the Science of Better Cooking came out from Chronicle Books in September 2026. It’s a good fit for the cook who keeps asking why a recipe calls for a specific step, and wants the answer along with dinner.

#41079. Tesla needs wireless charging fast, or its $30,000 Cybercab can’t charge at home

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1434 w)
📖 Baca
EV & Auto ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Electrek ↗ Open Full Page

Tesla needs wireless charging fast, or its $30,000 Cybercab can’t charge at home

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1434 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, tesla is now taking orders for the $29,990 Cybercab, with the first deliveries expected in Austin next month.
  • Recent findings suggest that the Cybercab has no onboard charger, so it only takes DC fast charging.
  • In a recent development, when Tesla unveiled the Cybercab in 2024, Elon Musk stated it wouldn’t even have a plug.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, tesla is now taking orders for the $29,990 Cybercab, with the first deliveries expected in Austin next month. But there’s a problem buyers should know about: they won’t be able to charge it at home.

Recent findings suggest that the Cybercab has no onboard charger, so it only takes DC fast charging. And the wireless home charging pad Tesla has been teasing since 2023 still isn’t something you can buy.

In a recent development, when Tesla unveiled the Cybercab in 2024, Elon Musk stated it wouldn’t even have a plug. “It just goes over the inductive charger and charges,” he said on stage.

Industry observers note that that strategy didn’t survive production, or at least the current version in production. Cybercabs have a NACS charge port behind a panel in the rear bumper, and Tesla has been plugging Cybercabs into regular Superchargers in Austin since they joined the fleet.

The bigger issue is what sits behind that port. Tesla confirmed to attendees at Tesla’s Austin launch event in September that Cybercab has no onboard charger, the box that turns the AC power coming out of your wall into DC power the battery can store.

Sources indicate that no onboard charger means no Wall Connector. No Mobile Connector on a 120V outlet, and no Level 2 station at the mall either. If it isn’t a DC fast charger, the Cybercab can’t use it.

Industry observers note that for a robotaxi, deleting the onboard charger makes sense. It’s one less part to buy, cool, and carry around, and a fleet car spends its downtime at a depot, not in someone’s garage. Those little things help make the car more economical and efficient.

But Tesla is now selling the Cybercab to individuals.

Industry observers note that as we reported last week, Tesla’s Cybercab autonomy agreement requires a $299 monthly subscription for the car to move at all. The same document puts charging squarely on the buyer: “You are responsible for registration, insurance, parking, charging, general cleaning and all other costs.”.

It also tells owners to “keep the vehicle charged and connected so over-the-air updates can install.” Connected to what, it doesn’t say.

The Cybercab Order Agreement limits the car to NACS DC fast charging, Superchargers included. It also says only the registered owner can use the Cybercab, and only while physically present in it for the entire trip.

The subscription agreement carves out one exception: when service is due, the Cybercab “will travel autonomously, unoccupied to a Tesla service center.” Nothing similar exists for charging.

Industry observers note that so you can’t send your Cybercab to a Supercharger at 2 a.m. while you sleep, which is the one thing a self-driving car should be great at. You’d have to ride along, sit in a two-seater at a Supercharger while it charges, and ride back home.

The obvious answer is the wireless home charger Tesla keeps promising.

It has been revealed that tesla first highlighted what looked like a wireless home charging station during its Investor Day in March 2023. Later that year, chief designer Franz von Holzhausen confirmed the project on Jay Leno’s Garage, saying owners would “just drive over the pad in your garage” to start charging.

Tesla then filed patents for the charging pad and, after the Cybercab unveiling, released a video of it charging the robotaxi at 25 kW, claiming efficiency “well above 90%.” In February, the FCC granted Tesla a waiver to use ultra-wideband radios to guide the Cybercab onto the pad.

Industry observers note that and that’s where it stops. Tesla has never sold the pad, never priced it, and never given it a launch date. It even gave up on wireless charging for the Cybertruck last year, even though the truck shipped with the connectors for it.

With deliveries estimated for December, Tesla has about six weeks to launch a home pad if it wants the first owners to charge in their own garage.

Recent findings suggest that tesla’s own aims for Cybercab charging revolve around fleet depots. In Austin, it filed plans for a hub on St. Elmo Road with 48 V4 Supercharger stalls in a first phase and cabinets to support 80 wireless chargers in a second.

Tesla could, in theory, let private owners use it. But with the owner-presence rule, that means riding to a depot across town and waiting there. That’s a Supercharger visit with extra steps.

The other route is a home DC charger, and those exist. We covered Sigenergy’s 25 kW bidirectional DC charging module last year, which bypasses a car’s onboard charger the same way a Supercharger does. Lunar Energy also announced a 25 kW home DC charger this year, but it’s not expected until mid-2027.

Neither is a plug-and-play answer. Sigenergy’s module is built to sit inside its SigenStor home battery system, which isn’t cheap, and Tesla would have to support third-party DC charging on a car it controls this tightly. Tesla could also build its own small DC wall unit. It hasn’t revealed one, but CEO Elon Musk talked about integrating one into the Powerwall for years.

This is what happens when you take a vehicle designed for a fleet and sell it to consumers to hit a deadline. And let’s be honest, charging is probably not even in the top 5 of problems with selling the Cybercab to personal owners in its current state.

It has been revealed that musk promised a Cybercab would be sold to a customer for under $30,000 before 2027. Technically, he’s going to make it. But on the Q3 earnings call, he also stated “the vast majority” of Cybercabs will stay Tesla-owned and run as transport-as-a-service. The car was clearly engineered around that, and deleting the onboard charger is the best example.

In a recent development, that saved Tesla money on every unit. The cost now lands on the few people buying one.

I don't see any evidence that the production Cybercab has the onboard hardware to use such a pad. Besides the wireless receiver coil it would need some kind of charging hardware to convert the pulsed wireless charging into DC to charge the battery.

Recent findings suggest that if you live in Austin next to a Supercharger, you’ll manage. But think about what Tesla is actually selling here: a self-driving car that can’t drive itself to charge, can’t charge in your garage, and needs you sitting in it at a Supercharger. That’s worse than owning a Model 3 with a Wall Connector, and it costs $299 a month on top.

It has been revealed that the fix exists in Tesla’s labs. It has the pad, the patents, and the FCC approval. It needs to ship it as a product, ideally bundled with the car, or change the contract to let the Cybercab go charge on its own.

Will the first Cybercab owners get a wireless pad in December, or will they spend their evenings at Superchargers? And if it rolls out, how much will it cost? The rare few home wireless chargers that have been sold to date have been quite expensive, and the value proposition of the Cybercab, which is right now basically a $300 a month lease with a $30,000 down payment, is already pretty awful.

Industry observers note that if you’re buying an EV, how you charge it at home matters as much as the car itself, and pairing it with rooftop solar can cut your fuel costs to nearly zero. With electricity rates up almost 10% last year and expected to keep climbing, going solar is one of the best ways to protect yourself against rising costs. And with lease and PPA options, you can do it with zero upfront cost and start saving immediately. If you want to find the best deal, check out EnergySage. #41078. Industry News: PUBG's extraction shooter spin-off, Black Budget, is finally going to be playable next month

📅 21 Nov 2025 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (409 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Vg247 ↗ Open Full Page

Industry News: PUBG's extraction shooter spin-off, Black Budget, is finally going to be playable next month

📅 21 Nov 2025 | ⏱️ 2 min read (409 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Vg247

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • You’d be forgiven for not remembering PUBG: Black Budget, the extraction off-shoot of the original battle royale shooter, PUBG.
  • This changes today, as the publisher - along with the game’s developer, PUBG Studios, have finally lifted the lid off the upcoming shooter.
  • Industry observers note that black Budget is described as a “tactical” extraction shooter.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

You’d be forgiven for not remembering PUBG: Black Budget, the extraction off-shoot of the original battle royale shooter, PUBG. Black Budget has been sort of floating around the internet for months, but Krafton never really committed to revealing core details about the game, or when players will actually get to play it.

This changes today, as the publisher - along with the game’s developer, PUBG Studios, have finally lifted the lid off the upcoming shooter.

Industry observers note that black Budget is described as a “tactical” extraction shooter. Squads of players infiltrate a mysterious island trapped in a time loop. There’s a bit of a STALKER element here with anomalies and various, unpredictable environmental shifts.

Recent findings suggest that coli, the island in question, hides a research facility that holds secrets and artefacts, which is what players will be attempting to extract. This is very much a PvPvE shooter, though PUBG Studios states the focus will be on exploration and discovery, rather than constant combat.

The game’s first set of closed alpha tests is set for December. The first takes place December 12-14, and another is scheduled for December 19-21. That’s six days across two weeks, with the test only being available on PC. Both sessions will be open to players in North America, Europe, and Asia.

Recent findings suggest that as it usually works with these sorts of tets on Steam, the game’s Steam page has a link where you can request access. If granted, you’ll be able to find the closed alpha in your library and download it when the time comes.

Industry observers note that though this is a closed test, Krafton confirmed that players will be able to capture and livestream their gameplay. In fact, watching content creators might be how you get access, as Black Budget is going to have a Twitch Drops event running alongside those sessions.

When I played Arc Raiders prior to its launch, I likened its tense and uncertain atmosphere to that of the early days of PUBG, so it’s going to be very interesting to see what actual PUBG does with the extraction shooter premise.

So far, it sounds like it’s going to be doing its own thing, leaning more into the adventure side of the subgenre, but we’ll have to see how it all shakes out when the tests start. Indeed, the BR-like constantly shrinking circle sounds like it could be a game-changing twist.

Losing Weight in Your 50s May Protect Your Heart Health Later in Life

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Losing weight in your 50s, even a modest amount, may help protect your heart health later in life, according to new research.Adults who lost weight in their early 50s saw their blood pressure, “good” cholesterol and inflammation change at about the same rate as adults who stayed at a healthy weight, according to a study from researchers at University College London and the University of Glasgow.Adults who gained weight in their early 50s saw those same measures worsen faster by their early 60s, the researchers reported.
  • Sources indicate that charis Bridger-Staatz, PhD, a senior research fellow at UCL, led the study.
  • The findings can apply to Americans because British and U.S.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Losing weight in your 50s, even a modest amount, may help protect your heart health later in life, according to new research.Adults who lost weight in their early 50s saw their blood pressure, “good” cholesterol and inflammation change at about the same rate as adults who stayed at a healthy weight, according to a study from researchers at University College London and the University of Glasgow.Adults who gained weight in their early 50s saw those same measures worsen faster by their early 60s, the researchers reported. The authors posted the study on a research-sharing website on September 4. Other scientists have not yet peer-reviewed the work.

Sources indicate that charis Bridger-Staatz, PhD, a senior research fellow at UCL, led the study. She told Healthline the main takeaway for adults over 50 was that “it’s not too late to try and do things that are going to improve your health.”Nearly half of U.S. adults ages 40 to 59 had obesity from 2021 to 2023, the highest rate of any adult age group, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). Among all U.S. adults, around 31.7% were overweight, according to the CDC.

The findings can apply to Americans because British and U.S. adults share similar weight patterns, said Solveig Cunningham, PhD, a professor of global health at Emory University’s Rollins School of Public Health. Cunningham, who was not involved in the research, told Healthline that Americans tend to gain weight across adulthood.

“By the time you get into your 50s, close to the majority of Americans already have obesity. Many others have overweight,” she mentioned.The World Health Organization (WHO) calls obesity a chronic disease. Healthcare professionals diagnose overweight and obesity using a person’s weight and height, or body mass index (BMI).

Bridger-Staatz said the team set out to learn who lost weight and kept it off before GLP-1 weight loss medications became available, and whether that weight loss improved health over time.

She said researchers had long assumed that “once people had become overweight or developed obesity, people didn’t really lose weight and certainly not sustained it.”The team also asked, she said, “can we try and say something positive about health that isn’t just this kind of like doom and gloom?”The researchers used the British 1958 National Child Development Study, which has followed about 17,500 people born during one week in 1958. Of those, 6,309 took part in a health check in their early 60s, according to the report.The team compared each person’s highest weight between ages 23 and 42 with their weight between ages 50 and 55. Researchers sorted people by whether they gained or lost more than 5% of their body weight and kept the change. For a 200-pound person, 5% equals 10 pounds.To track heart health, the team compared blood tests and blood pressure readings at ages 44 and 62 with those of people who maintained a healthy weight.“We know everyone’s heart health is kind of going to get a little bit worse over that time because you are aging and that’s expected,” Bridger-Staatz said. The question, she said, was, “Does it slow the rate at which people’s heart health is getting worse?”.

Weight loss slowed the decline in heart health for people who were overweight and for people with obesity, according to the report.People who were overweight and lost weight had the strongest positive results. By age 62, their body fat-to-lean tissue ratio matched that of the healthy-weight group. The authors wrote that differences in body fat may partly explain why weight changes affected heart health.People with obesity who lost weight had less body fat at 62 than people in the other obesity groups, according to the report.Sudhakara Chennareddy, MD, prevention cardiologist in the Center for Cardiovascular Prevention, Metabolism and Lipids at Georgia Heart Institute, told Healthline those results are what he’d expect. He was not involved in the research.“Even losing 5% has beneficial effects on the cardiovascular side effects,” he said. Long-term blood sugar was the exception. For people with obesity who lost weight, it rose more than in the healthy-weight group, though the authors reported that the result was not statistically significant.

A 2025 study of more than 15,000 U.S. adults, published in Endocrinology, Diabetes & Metabolism, found that adults who had previously had obesity tended to have higher blood sugar than those who had never had it, even after their BMI dropped.

“It’s not the patient’s fault… We need to treat this one like any other chronic disease, like we treat hypertension or we treat diabetes,” Chennareddy said.Compared with the healthy-weight group, people who gained weight in their early 50s had faster increases in blood pressure, blood fats, and inflammation, and declines in “good” cholesterol. Obesity is a chronic metabolic disease that leads to inflammation in the body, which can raise the risk of heart attack and stroke and worsen cholesterol levels, Chennareddy said. “The more weight they gain, they develop prediabetes and diabetes and fatty liver disease as well,” he said.These changes were largest for people who developed obesity or already had obesity and gained more weight, the researchers reported. This group also saw faster increases in long-term blood sugar levels.About 37% of participants gained more than 5% of their body weight in their early 50s. Only about 6% lost weight and kept it off, according to the study.“To me, that’s sort of the stronger message,” Cunningham said of the findings. Her advice for adults in their 50s is to avoid gaining weight.

People with obesity who lost and then gained the weight back saw faster drops in “good” cholesterol and faster rises in inflammation and long-term blood sugar.

Recent findings suggest that by age 62, they weighed slightly less, on average, than people whose obesity remained steady, according to the report’s data. They also carried more body fat and had more inflammation.Weight cycling can do more harm than steady weight, Chennareddy noted. He gave the example of someone who gains 20 pounds, loses 30 and then gains 20 again. “That is even more detrimental,” he said.When people lose weight, the body slows its resting metabolism, he said. When the weight comes back, “most of the weight they gain is fat, not muscle,” he said. Even someone who loses and regains 5% to 7% of their body weight may end up with slightly less muscle and more fat, he said.Some research has shown that weight fluctuation is associated with a higher risk of high blood pressure and cardiovascular disease-related death.

The study’s weight changes took place between about 2008 and 2013, according to the study’s timeline.

Recent findings suggest that wegovy, a GLP-1 medication for weight management, introduced in the United Kingdom in September 2023, according to the UK Department of Health and Social Care.Cunningham mentioned the weight-cycling findings raised questions for people who take GLP-1 medications. She said drugmakers’ own data show that “once you get off of those, your weight is going to go right back to where it was before, possibly even worse.”That could create the same up-and-down pattern, Cunningham said. She added that researchers don’t yet know “what happens in the really long term” for people who take these medications.

The study indicated links between weight changes and heart health and cannot prove that weight changes caused the results, according to the authors. They wrote that the small number of people who lost weight made those results less precise.Bridger-Staatz also remarked the team did not look at why or how people lost weight.

Cunningham mentioned adults lose muscle and bone mass with age, and that the loss is especially pronounced for women in their 50s and older. “Maintaining muscles and maintaining bones is so, so important,” she said.Staying active helps people keep muscle, even without weight loss, Cunningham said. “Even a little bit of activity…just keep moving,” she said.GLP-1 medications work best as part of a “comprehensive strategy,” Chennareddy said. With his patients, he said he recommends continuous improvement rather than setting a goal to lose a specific amount of weight within a set period.Patients who treat weight loss as “a gradual process” do better long term, he said.“The most important thing is not to do fad diets,” Chennareddy said.For people losing weight, Chennareddy recommended:.

Anyone considering changes to their weight can talk with a healthcare professional about their weight history and goals.
